synopsis: The Soil Contact Model (SCM) is a semi-empirical terramechanics approach used to represent braking force and sinkage on soft ground [f6096, f6461, f13834]. Chapters 5 and 8 place SCM within Chrono's terrain capabilities, describing Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage modelling alongside rigid terrain and more computationally expensive granular or deformable alternatives; Chapter 8 also identifies shear parameters [f3961, f6014]. The SCM authors claim in a peer-reviewed paper that their open-source model runs as fast as empirical models while offering fidelity “comparable” to discrete-element methods [f6097, f6463]. That performance comparison is an attributed author claim: the supplied facts provide no quantitative benchmark or independent confirmation [f6097, f6463].

relations.note: Both describe Chrono's terrain options, including SCM with Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage.
Both identify semi-empirical terramechanics as representing soft-soil braking force and sinkage.
Both attribute DEM-comparable fidelity to SCM's authors.
Adds Bekker-Wong and Altair soft soil as alternative models.
Identifies Bekker-Wong alongside SCM within the semi-empirical model class.
Adds shear parameters and the higher cost of granular or deformable alternatives.
Adds empirical-model speed, open-source status, and peer-reviewed provenance to the fidelity claim.
